findings.criterion: clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal
findings.message: The North Star explicitly mandates that 'clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal'. Phase 3 introduces a 'Two-step tile affordance' where the first click only opens a passive warm view, requiring a second 'Resume live' click to actually spawn the terminal. This directly violates the single-click-to-terminal requirement.

Phase 7 specifies a live drift tripwire that uses 'report.warn (never red)' if sidecar parsing fails on real files. If the upstream provider changes their sidecar format, parsing will fail, and Anchor will silently record zero usage for all new sessions while the pipeline remains 'green'. This directly violates 'not zero-by-omission' by allowing silent omission.

findings.criterion: clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal
findings.message: Phase 6 introduces 'oldest-first graceful eviction' for parked worktrees, but fails to define how clicking an evicted session's tile will 'reliably open a warm terminal'. If the underlying worktree is deleted, the plan lacks a mechanism to reconstruct the PTY state and narrate the session, risking a broken or blank terminal upon click.

findings.criterion: Every Anchor session — interactive ConPTY or one-shot job... clicking ANY session tile reliably opens a warm terminal
findings.message: The North Star requires both 'interactive ConPTY' and 'one-shot job' sessions to reliably open a warm terminal on tile click. While Phase 4 captures cost for one-shot jobs, Phase 6's Playwright screenshot sign-off completely omits one-shot jobs from the tile classes it tests, leaving the terminal requirement unverified for these sessions.

The plan explicitly defers Gemini usage capture to a fast-follow. While multi-model support is desirable for future-proofing, the North Star does not mandate specific backend engines, only that the sessions that do run leave an honest trail. This is a known, documented deferral.
